answer: Practically, the chain should pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because harbor only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, velvet is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any nadir approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
